activity.notes: Ahmad ibn Majid was an Arab navigator and author associated with Julfar and the western Indian Ocean in the later fifteenth century. Library of Congress authority data gives an activity range of 1462-1498, while archaeology places Julfar within the Hormuzi political-commercial sphere in this period. ATLAS therefore uses Kingdom of Hormuz as the representative political context with approximate boundaries. It does not repeat the disputed later claim that Ibn Majid personally piloted Vasco da Gama to India.

sources.citation_text: The Library of Congress authority record identifies Aḥmad ibn Mājid as an Arab navigator and gives an activity range of 1462-1498, with a major navigational compilation dated 1490.

sources.title: The Archaeology of Julfar — UCL Discovery
sources.citation_text: Archaeological scholarship on Julfar places the port within the wider Hormuzi political and commercial system in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries.
